summary: Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist who studied at Keble College, Oxford (~1923–1927). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1950) and was a visiting professor at the University of Washington (~1959–1961).

Hugh Falconer worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1822–1826) and the University of Edinburgh (~1826–1829), later serving as Superintendent at Saharanpur (1832) and Calcutta Botanic Gardens, alongside Calcutta Medical College (1848–1855).

Hugh George Rawlinson was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned an M.A. at Emmanuel College (~1899–1903). His career included posts at Karnatak Arts College (1917–1923) and Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1917–1933).
Hugh Gray was an Indologist who studied at Battersea Grammar School. He served as a lecturer at the University of London and SOAS University of London around 1964 to 1970.

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who completed his doctorate at Stanford University (~1969–1973). He was a professor at Stony Brook University from 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1980–2013).

Hugh Trevor Lambrick was an Indologist and historian who earned his B.A. (~1923–1926) and D.Litt. (1971) at Oxford, where he also held posts at Oriel College as Fellow (1947) and Lecturer in Modern History (1951).
Hugh van Skyhawk is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer. He served as Professor of Comparative Religion at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2008).

Hugo David is an Indologist and philosopher who completed a PhD at École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held a Newton International Fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2015.

Hugo Ehrlich was a linguist who studied at the University of Jena and under Karl Brugmann at the University of Leipzig (~1897–1901). In 1912, he was a Privatdozent for Indogermanistik at the University of Königsberg.

Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held a post at Sophia University around 1935 and studied under the traditional teacher Koun Yamada (~1970–1989).

Hugo Heinrich Figulla was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Berlin and Breslau (under Bruno Meissner). He served at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1934–1936) and as a Keeper at the British Museum (1946–1963).

Hugo Schuchardt was a linguist who studied under August Schleicher and Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, earning a Ph.D. at Bonn. He served as professor of Romance philology at Halle-Wittenberg (1873) and the University of Graz (1876–1900).
Hugo Valvanne was an Indology scholar who earned his M.A. at the University of Helsinki, where he studied under J. N. Reuter from approximately 1912 to 1917.
Hugo Winckler was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883–1887) and later held an academic post there from around 1891 to 1913.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He held posts at Taipei National University of the Arts (~1992), Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and served as President of Dharma Drum Institute (~2014–2022).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kuo-wei Liu, and also studied under teachers Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin and studied under the traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University (attested 1996).
